about: Every recorded line in the games. The name on the left is the sound file; the words on the right are what the voice says. To change a line: edit the words, delete its sound file, and run tools/make-voice.py again. Only missing files are recorded, so nothing is paid for twice. A character whose voice id below is empty has not been given a voice yet, and their lines wait.

audio/g2/lesson/try-them-in-sentences-th: Try them in sentences. The sand is hot. The snow is cold.
audio/g2/lesson/some-words-mean-the-same: Some words mean the same thing. Big and large mean the same.

audio/g2/lesson/a-naming-word-called-a-n: A naming word, called a noun, names a person, a place or a thing. Here's a test: can you put 'the' in front of it? The pyramid. Yes! It's a noun.
audio/g2/lesson/an-action-word-called-a-: An action word, called a verb, is something you do. Test it: can you say 'I can' in front of it? I can dig. Yes! It's a verb.
audio/g2/lesson/a-describing-word-called: A describing word, called an adjective, tells us what something is like. A golden crown. Golden tells us what the crown is like.
audio/g2/lesson/a-scribe-had-to-spell-ev: A scribe had to spell every word the right way. Let's try!
audio/g2/lesson/some-sounds-are-spelled-: Some sounds are spelled with a team of letters. In rain, the A and the I work together to make the long A sound. In boat, O A makes the long O sound. In night, I G H makes the long I sound.
audio/g2/lesson/and-in-cake-the-e-at-the: And in cake, the E at the end is silent. It makes the A say its name.
audio/g2/lesson/some-words-have-a-tricky: Some words have a tricky part that doesn't sound the way it looks. We call them heart words, because we learn the tricky part by heart.
audio/g2/lesson/in-friend-the-tricky-par: In friend, the tricky part is I E. Look at it, say the letters, and remember it: F, R, I, E, N, D.
audio/g2/lesson/to-mean-more-than-one-mo: To mean more than one, most words just add S. One cat, two cats.
audio/g2/lesson/words-that-end-in-s-x-s-: Words that end in S, X, S H or C H add E S. One box, two boxes.
audio/g2/lesson/if-a-word-ends-in-a-cons: If a word ends in a consonant and Y, change the Y to I and add E S. One baby, two babies.
audio/g2/lesson/and-some-words-change-co: And some words change completely. One mouse, two mice!
audio/g2/lesson/to-talk-about-yesterday-: To talk about yesterday, most words add E D. Today I jump. Yesterday I jumped.
audio/g2/lesson/short-words-like-stop-do: Short words like stop double the last letter first. Stopped.
